subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find dy/dx for x = a((1 − t²)/(1 + t²)), y = 2bt/(1 + t²).

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what makes it a parametric problem and how you reach dy/dx.

steps.label: State the parametric rule
steps.margin_note: First mark. The rule itself earns it, so write it before differentiating anything. The substitution t = tan θ is a choice, not a rule — say that you are making it.
lines: Both x and y are given through the parameter t, so
(t = tan θ, with θ in (−π/2, π/2), gives every real t;

lines.text: by the chain rule dy/dx = (dy/dθ)/(dx/dθ) as well)

lines: Any parameter may be used. Put t = tan θ, so that

recall.must_convey: That dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt) for a parametric pair, and that t = tan θ is being substituted.
accept: x and y are both in terms of t so dy by dx is dy by dt over dx by dt
use the parametric rule and put t equal to tan theta
differentiate both with respect to the parameter and divide
parametric rule rasi, t ni tan theta ga substitute cheyyali
state the chain rule for a parameter first

steps.why: Neither x nor y is written in terms of the other, so the derivative has to be reached through the parameter. Writing the rule earns the method mark even if the algebra afterwards slips.
common_mistakes: Differentiating y with respect to t and calling that dy/dx.
Writing dy/dx = (dx/dt)/(dy/dt), the two the wrong way round.
steps.memory_tip: The dt cancels in (dy/dt)/(dx/dt) — that cancellation tells you the fraction is the right way up.

steps.label: Substitute t = tan θ
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Both standard forms follow from 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ: (1 − tan²θ)/(1 + tan²θ) = cos 2θ and 2 tan θ/(1 + tan²θ) = sin 2θ.

recall.must_convey: That the substitution turns x into a cos 2θ and y into b sin 2θ.
accept: x becomes a cos two theta and y becomes b sin two theta
use the tan half angle forms of sin two theta and cos two theta
after substituting the point is on an ellipse
x a cos two theta avuthundi, y b sin two theta avuthundi
both reduce to single trigonometric terms

steps.why: These are the standard tan-half-angle forms of cos 2θ and sin 2θ. Once they are used, x and y are single trigonometric terms and each differentiates in one line.
common_mistakes: Writing 2 tan θ/(1 + tan²θ) as tan 2θ instead of sin 2θ.
Using (1 − tan²θ)/(1 + tan²θ) = cos θ instead of cos 2θ.
steps.memory_tip: Both forms carry 2θ: numerator 2 tan θ gives sin 2θ, numerator 1 − tan²θ gives cos 2θ.

steps.label: Differentiate with respect to θ
steps.margin_note: Third mark. The factor 2 comes from the chain rule on 2θ and cancels between the two derivatives, so only the sign and b/a are left.

recall.must_convey: That dx/dθ = −2a sin 2θ, dy/dθ = 2b cos 2θ and dividing gives −(b/a) cot 2θ.
accept: differentiate both and divide to get minus b over a cot two theta
dx by d theta is minus two a sin two theta
dy by d theta is two b cos two theta
rendintini theta tho differentiate chesi divide cheyyali
the twos cancel and cos over sin gives cot

steps.why: Dividing cos 2θ by sin 2θ gives cot 2θ, so the result is one short term instead of the long quotient that the direct method gives.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the factor 2 from the chain rule on 2θ.
Losing the minus sign that comes from differentiating cos 2θ.
steps.memory_tip: cos over sin is cot, sin over cos is tan — the answer here is a cot because cos 2θ is on top.

steps.label: Write the answer in t
steps.margin_note: Last mark. The answer must return to t, because the question is set in t. −(1 − t²) = t² − 1, so the two written forms are the same.

recall.must_convey: That cot 2θ is rewritten in t and the answer is b(t² − 1)/(2at).
accept: convert cot two theta back into t and get b times t squared minus one over two a t
the answer is b t squared minus one divided by two a t
put tan theta equal to t again
chivarilo t lo ne answer rayali
cot two theta is one minus t squared over two t

steps.why: A parametric answer is expected in the parameter the question uses. Leaving θ in the final line answers a different question.
common_mistakes: Leaving the answer in θ when the question is set in t.
Writing cot 2θ as 2t/(1 − t²), which is tan 2θ.
steps.memory_tip: Check at t = 1: the point is (0, b), the top of the ellipse, where the tangent is horizontal — and the answer gives dy/dx = 0.

insider_note: Put t = tan θ and the point becomes (a cos2θ, b sin2θ) — an ellipse — so both derivatives are one line. Differentiating the fractions in t directly is far heavier.
